Empirical Research Plan  
“How do frictions in the shadow-banking sector affect the lending behavior of U.S. money-market funds (MMFs)?”

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with an event-study extension (Sun-Abraham 2020 estimator).

Rationale  
• We observe the same funds before and after a plausibly exogenous shock that tightened shadow-banking frictions—the Lehman/Reserve Primary Fund “break-the-buck” episode and the ensuing freeze of asset-backed commercial paper (ABCP) markets in September 2008.  
• Funds differed ex-ante in their exposure to that market (e.g., the pre-crisis share of ABCP and repo claims on broker-dealers).  
• Hence the shock is common in calendar time, but its bite is heterogeneous across funds.  
• Parallel-trend tests and flexible event-time coefficients can be implemented because we have 20+ months of pre-treatment data and 28 months post-treatment.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
────────────────────────────────────────
Unit of observation: fund-month i,t.

Treatment variable  
Treated_i = 1 if fund i’s exposure to shadow-banking instruments in 2007:M1-2008:M6 (pre-period) is in the top quartile of the distribution:
 Exposure_i = average( share of ABCP + unsecured repo + broker-dealer time deposits ).

Control group  
Funds in the bottom quartile of Exposure_i (“low-exposure” funds).

(Results will be re-estimated with Exposure_i as a continuous measure and with the median split as robustness.)

Treatment timing  
Event month τ = 2008-09. Post_t = 1 for all months ≥ 2008-09.

Event-study specification will include relative months k = –18 … +28.

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Parallel Trends: Absent the September-2008 disruption, high- and low-exposure funds would have followed parallel lending trajectories.  
 Plausibility: Prior to Lehman, ABCP markets were liquid; regulatory regime identical. Pre-trend graphs can be inspected.

A2. Exogeneity of Exposure: A fund’s 2007–H1 2008 exposure was chosen before anyone foresaw the specific Lehman run severity.  
 Plausibility: Manager style is sticky; hard to foresee the timing/intensity of the freeze.

A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value (no spillovers): A high-exposure fund’s contraction does not mechanically force a low-exposure fund to expand (we will test for market-share reallocation).  
 Plausibility: The MMF sector is large, but individual funds are small relative to the market; still, we will control for category-level flows.

A4. No Differential Composition Changes: Entry/exit is limited; we will drop funds that liquidate mid-sample and re-weight by pre-period AUM.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations
────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Anticipation or gradual build-up of stress in summer-2008  
 Mitigation: Re-estimate using 2008-07 as alternative event date; include fund*linear time trends; conduct placebo tests using 2007-09 “fake” treatment.

T2. Sort-on-shock: Funds may adjust exposure between 2008-07 and 2008-09.  
 Mitigation: Define exposure using only holdings ≤ 2007-12; freeze sample; show that reclassification using 2008-Q2 holdings leaves results unchanged.

T3. Time-varying confounders (e.g., sponsor support lines, bank affiliation).  
 Mitigation: Add interactions of Post_t with sponsor-type fixed effects; include fund*month flows and market-wide ABCP yield spreads as controls; perform a triple-DiD using off-balance-sheet support announcements.

────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────
```r
#---------------- Setup ----------------#
library(data.table)
library(fixest)          # fast fe regressions
library(did)             # Sun & Abraham implementation
options(fixest_progress = FALSE)

#---------------- 1. Load data ----------------#
mmf <- fread("mmf_monthly_2007_2011.csv")   # one row per fund-month

#---------------- 2. Variable construction ----------------#
# Pre-period exposure: average Jan 2007 – Jun 2008
pre_period <- mmf[date >= "2007-01-01" & date <= "2008-06-30",
                  .(exposure = mean(abcp_share + repo_share + bd_td_share, na.rm=TRUE)),
                  by = fund_id]

# Merge back
mmf <- merge(mmf, pre_period, by="fund_id")

# Treatment indicator
q75 <- quantile(mmf$exposure, .75, na.rm=TRUE)
q25 <- quantile(mmf$exposure, .25, na.rm=TRUE)

mmf[, treated := fifelse(exposure >= q75, 1L,
                  fifelse(exposure <= q25, 0L, NA_integer_))]

# Keep only high vs low exposure funds
mmf <- mmf[!is.na(treated)]

# Event timing
mmf[, post := as.integer(date >= "2008-09-01")]

# Relative month k for event study
mmf[, rel_month := as.integer((as.yearmon(date) - as.yearmon("2008-09"))*12)]

# Outcome: log lending amount (e.g., repos + CP)
mmf[, log_lend := log1p(total_lending)]

#---------------- 3. Main DID regression ----------------#
did_main <- feols(log_lend ~ treated*post + fund_size + flow_rate |
                  fund_id + month, data = mmf, cluster = ~fund_id)

etable(did_main)

#---------------- 4. Event-study (Sun-Abraham) -----------#
library(did)
sa <- att_gt(yname   = "log_lend",
             tname   = "date",     # in Date or numeric
             idname  = "fund_id",
             gname   = "event_time", # first treated date (2008-09 for treated, Inf otherwise)
             xformla = ~ fund_size + flow_rate,
             data    = mmf)

es <- aggte(sa, type="dynamic")
summary(es)
plot(es)

#---------------- 5. Robustness: continuous exposure -----#
mmf[, treat_intensity := scale(exposure)]

feols(log_lend ~ treat_intensity*post + fund_size + flow_rate |
      fund_id + month, data = mmf, cluster = ~fund_id)
```
(The file mmf_monthly_2007_2011.csv is assumed to contain fund_id, date, portfolio shares, total_lending, AUM, flows, etc.)

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────
Theory predicts that tighter shadow-bank frictions (ABCP market freeze) reduce the willingness or ability of highly exposed MMFs to roll over credit.  
Direction: β̂ (treated × post) < 0.  
Magnitude (back-of-the-envelope): a 10 p.p. higher pre-crisis shadow exposure could cut post-crisis lending growth by ≈ 5–8 percent per month relative to controls, cumulating to a 40 percent lower stock by 2011.

Implications: contraction spills over to corporate CP borrowers and short-term funding markets, amplifying systemic stress.

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)
────────────────────────────────────────
C1: Parallel pre-trends visually & statistically supported……… 1  
C2: No anticipation of the exact Lehman shock………………… 1  
C3: Stable composition (limited entry/exit; balanced panel)…… 0.8  
C4: No spillovers between treatment & control………………… 0.7  
C5: Consistent timing of shock across units…………………… 1  
Overall (average)………………………………………………… 0.9

────────────────────────────────────────
End of empirical plan
